properties.displayName: Azure - Control Plane Activity from Previously Unseen IP
properties.description:
DETECTS
Azure control-plane operations originating from a caller IP address not seen anywhere in the previous 14 days.

WHY IT MATTERS
Behavioural baseline rather than a signature. Administrative activity normally originates from a stable set of egress IPs. A brand-new source IP performing control-plane operations is consistent with credential theft, session hijack, or access from attacker infrastructure (MITRE T1078, Valid Accounts). Effective against attackers who hold valid credentials and would otherwise generate no failures.

TRIAGE
1. Geolocate the new IP and compare against expected admin locations.
2. Review the operations performed. Read-only enumeration differs sharply from write or delete.
3. Check the Caller sign-in history for a matching new IP in SigninLogs.
4. Confirm with the user whether they changed network, travelled, or started using a new VPN.
5. If unexplained: revoke sessions and force reauthentication.

FALSE POSITIVES
New VPN endpoints, ISP address changes, travel, and newly deployed automation. Expect noise during the first 14 days of operation while the baseline fills.

SOURCE
AzureActivity
properties.query:
let KnownCallerIps = AzureActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(14d) .. ago(1d))
    | where isnotempty(CallerIpAddress)
    | distinct CallerIpAddress;
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where isnotempty(CallerIpAddress)
| where CallerIpAddress !in (KnownCallerIps)
| summarize OperationCount = count(), Operations = make_set(OperationNameValue, 20),
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated), EndTime = max(TimeGenerated)
    by Caller, CallerIpAddress
| extend TimeGenerated = EndTime, Account = Caller, IP = CallerIpAddress
